Marketplace Coordination Demo: How Platforms Reduce Idle Time

One city and one 10-driver pool, two operating models. The left panel shows customers facing expensive, less certain street-style service while drivers burn time waiting at stands. The right panel coordinates matching, ordering, and payment so more customers can afford to take trips and drivers can either finish sooner for the same pay or stay out and earn more.

Takeaway

Coordination makes the market better for both customers and drivers

Better coordination lowers customer price, raises availability, and removes ordering friction. Those customer gains feed directly into less wasted driver time and better pay choices.

Customer win More affordable, more available rides

When rides are easier to order and cheaper to buy, more customers choose to travel.

Driver win Less wasted time, better pay options

Saved idle time can become free personal time for the same pay or extra income if drivers stay out.

Model note Illustrative, not operational data

This widget uses a deterministic toy city, toy customer-pricing math, and simple availability / convenience scoring to show how dispatch coordination changes the economics of the same fleet.
